did_you_know.text: Did you know? David begins the psalm with two central values—lovingkindness and justice—and declares that he will sing and make music to the Lord about both.

Did you know? David asks for wisdom to follow the way of integrity—that is, to understand how to conduct himself in an upright and blameless way—and emphasizes that this conduct begins in his own household as well.
Did you know? The question “When will you come to me?” expresses David’s longing for the Lord’s presence and help as he walks in the way of integrity.
Did you know? David declares that he will not set any “worthless thing”—anything negative or corrupt—before his eyes, and adds that he keeps away from straying from the straight path.

Did you know? David seeks to distance himself from a “perverse heart” and refuses to associate with evil; thus, the psalm emphasizes that both the qualities of the heart and a person’s actions are subject to examination.
Did you know? David rejects secret slander, haughty eyes, and a proud heart; these three expressions describe hurtful speech and arrogance.

Did you know? In contrast to the corrupt people mentioned earlier, David wants the faithful in the land and those who walk in the way of integrity to live with him, and he says that they will serve him.

Did you know? According to the psalm, David’s household is no place for anyone who practices deceit or speaks lies; deceit and falsehood are presented as incompatible with stability and presence in the household.
Did you know? David describes an action repeated every morning: removing the wicked and evildoers from the land and from the city of the Lord, as part of an ongoing administration of justice.
